To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the current mobile computing model is inadequate and must be replaced by a new model that is based on a pervasive application model.
pervasive computing is a vision that will not be fully realized until the mobile community addresses the challenges of device heterogeneity, application portability, and context-awareness.

pervasive computing is a vision that can be realized by using the following three attributes of an application model: (i) the application model must be based on an environment-centric view of the application; (ii) the application must be able to dynamically adapt to changes in its environment; (iii) the application must have the ability to learn from its environment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new technologies and techniques that will make pervasive computing a reality.
the following questions: How do we make it easier to create applications that take advantage of pervasive computing?

the following: (1) the design of a new application programming interface (API) that allows applications to be developed in a manner that is not dependent on specific device characteristics; (2) the design of middleware that supports the new API; (3) the design of new application development and deployment tools that support the new API; and (4) the design of an environment that supports the execution of applications developed for the new API.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
pervasive computing will be a reality when a user can interact with a device in the same manner as he or she interacts with a person.
the pervasive computing model is a model of computing where a device or a set of devices is used to access information, applications, and services that are located in the environment of the user.
the current model for mobile computing is inadequate and a new model for pervasive computing must be developed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the mobile computing community must develop new models for pervasive computing that are based upon the user, rather than on devices, and that are based upon applications that are not device-specific, but are instead context-sensitive and context-aware.
we are developing a framework for the design and development of applications for pervasive computing.
we are trying to build a system that is aware of a person's environment and can provide services based on that knowledge.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a new model of applications is needed that is based on an application's role, rather than on the device that runs it.
the application model is the key enabler for the pervasive computing vision.
the mobile computing community must embrace a new application model for pervasive and ubiquitous computing that is based on the concept of a user's environment, not on the concept of the device.
